title: Sub-lemma B (sufficiency): each coordinate of F vanishes for product lambda as a polynomial identity for ALL generic A

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Claim ($\Leftarrow$).** If $\lambda_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}=u_\alpha v_\beta w_\gamma x_\delta$ on all non-identical cells, then $\mathbf F(\lambda_c Q^{(c)})=0$.

**What must be proved.** Each coordinate of $\mathbf F$, by Sub-lemma A, equals (up to a generically nonzero $A$-factor) a Segre $2\times2$ minor of $\lambda$, which vanishes identically when $\lambda$ is a pure product. Crucially this must hold **as a polynomial identity in $A$ for all Zariski-generic $A$**, not merely at sampled $A$: a coordinate is a polynomial in the $A^{(t)}$ that vanishes on a Zariski-dense set $\Rightarrow$ it vanishes identically. Invoke the polynomial-identity-from-dense-vanishing principle and the First Fundamental Theorem of invariant theory (bracket/Pl\"ucker algebra) to justify the cancellations are exact, not approximate.

**Failure mode to avoid (F3/F1).** Asserting vanishing from numerical evidence; conflating 'generic $A$' with 'all $A$'.
